To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Community Resilient Learning Collaborative and Resilience Network (C-LEAN) is a community-based, multi-sector, randomized, comparative effectiveness trial to determine how to best build service program and individual capacity to improve mental and physical health-related quality of live among individuals at risk of depression, with exposure social risk factors or environmental hazards, in communities at risk for events, such as hurricanes and other storms.

this study will test the effectiveness of a two-level intervention for building resilience to address depression and social risk factors, with a community engagement and planning component to enhance community capacity to support service programs and individual clients.

the Community Resilient Learning Collaborative and Network (C-LEAR) is a randomized comparative effectiveness trial to determine the effects of community engagement, planning and multi-sector coalition support on program-level implementation of a community-prioritized toolkit to build resilience to social risk factors and disaster response.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and evaluation of interventions to promote resilience and reduce the burden of mental illness in communities with high rates of depression and social risk factors and concerns about environmental hazards.
how community engagement, coalition building, and individual-level interventions can improve mental health-related QOL in the face of social risk and environmental threats.

the development and evaluation of community-based interventions that promote mental health and resilience among individuals who have been exposed to environmental hazards, social risk factors for mental illness, and/or who live in areas with high risk of natural disasters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

C-LEARN will use a community-based participatory research approach to develop and implement a randomized trial of a multi-level intervention to build individual resilience and community capacity to address social risk, depression, and environmental hazards in communities at risk for disasters.

C-LEARN aims to build community capacity to improve mental and physical health and quality of life through a multi-sector, multi-level approach to address depression, social risk, and disaster preparedness and responses.

the Community Resilient Learning Collaborative and Resiliency Network study protocol with participatory planning for a randomized, comparative effectiveness trial was developed to determine how to improve mental health related quality of life among adults at risk for depression with exposure to social and environmental risk factors in areas of Southern LA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the study is designed to test whether a multi-sector, multi-level, community-based intervention to address social risk and disaster preparedness and to enhance mental health-related quality-of-life is feasible and acceptable in communities at risk for depression.
the C-LEARN study is designed to build on the strengths of communities to improve mental health and resilience in the face of adversity.
we have a study protocol for a randomized comparative effectiveness trial that is based on a participatory planning process with community stakeholders.

the CPPR process can provide an effective means for community engagement and participatory research to identify community priorities and assets and to inform the design and implementation of community-based interventions to address community needs.
the participatory planning process was essential for building community capacity and buy-in for the study.
